findings.summary: The crew MCP tool's action Literal (line 2224) and parameter list still omit queue-edit, queue-reprioritise and queue-drop and the brief_path, done_when, time_budget, backend, model and priority arguments, so the three actions answer through crew_action() but cannot be reached through the MCP surface a coordinator actually calls; the rows needed are written out in the source run's required-out-of-scope-edits.md section 1, and the file is outside this node's fence.

No STATE_PHRASES rows exist for queue edit, queue reprioritise or queue drop, so the done-when clause 'the CLI help-contract tests cover the three verbs' is unmet and the census now names four unregistered leaves where it named one at base; the three rows are transcribed in tests/test_queue_verbs.py:404 and in required-out-of-scope-edits.md section 2, and the file is outside this node's fence.

The single-run-verb sweep reaches the three new leaves and raises KeyError at line 168 for each because MINIMAL_OPTIONS has no row for them, adding three failing parametrisations at the reviewed head that did not fail at base; the delta gate's population excludes this file by construction because it imports neither changed module, and required-out-of-scope-edits.md section 3 names the exact rows owed.

drop re-reads the pointer and checks only its own unlocked waiting-phase read; unlike edit (line 256) and reprioritise (line 320) it takes no pointer lock and repeats no phase check before crew.discard, which guards only on a live recorded pid, so the commit body's and the landing fragment's claim that every verb re-checks the phase under the lock is false for the one destructive verb.

The module docstring (lines 33-36) states that the queued path writes steering.md at queue time and admission reads it at launch, but nothing outside this module writes or reads steering.md at this head, so the claim describes the sibling binding node rather than this tree, and an edit's brief_sha256 names the new text while dispatch will store a copy of node.brief instead of it at launch.
